title: NFA to DFA: subset construction
overview: Follow all three source examples: make missing behavior explicit, combine branching possibilities into subsets, and build the final five-state DFA from its transition table.
objectives: Represent each DFA state as a set of NFA states.
Compute each subset transition by unioning destinations for every alphabet symbol.
Continue until all reachable subsets are processed.
Mark subsets containing an NFA final state as accepting.
Include and correctly loop the empty-set trap state when reachable/required.

keyTerms.definition: An automaton that can have several or no destinations for a state-symbol pair.
A conversion where each DFA state represents a set of NFA states.
A subset reached from the start subset by some input string.
A subset containing at least one accepting NFA state.
The set with no NFA states; each symbol maps it back to itself.

segments.title: Conversion keeps the same language
notes: An NFA and its equivalent DFA accept the same set of words. Their transition rules have different codomains: a DFA chooses one state, while an NFA may return a subset of states.
Subset construction records all NFA possibilities after one input prefix inside a single DFA state. It does not choose an arbitrary branch and discard the others.
segments.speakerNotes: Ang target ay equivalent DFA: pareho pa rin ang accepted strings. Sa DFA, isang destination; sa NFA, set ng mga posibleng states.
segments.visualDescription: The opening comparison displays the DFA/NFA transition mappings before the worked examples.

segments.title: Example 1: read the NFA for words starting with 0
notes: The first source example has start A, accepting B, a 0-edge A→B, and 0/1 loops at B. There is no 1-transition from A.
Its NFA table is A:[{B},∅], B:[{B},{B}] under columns 0 and 1. It accepts 0 and any suffix after that first 0; ε and words beginning with 1 are rejected.
segments.speakerNotes: Sa unang example, 0 ang unang symbol para makapunta sa B. Final ang B at may loop sa 0 at 1. Walang destination mula A sa input 1.
segments.visualDescription: At the checked 4:30–6:30 frames, the NFA and its table are introduced and filled.

segments.title: Name the missing destination as a dead state
notes: The DFA needs one destination for A on input 1. The source introduces C to represent the empty subset ∅. A therefore goes to B on 0 and C on 1.
C is rejecting and returns to itself on both symbols: once no NFA path remains, reading more input cannot restore one.
segments.speakerNotes: Ang walang destination ay papalitan ng dead state C sa complete DFA. Mula A sa 1, C ang pupuntahan; ang C ay hindi final.
segments.visualDescription: The NFA table and new DFA table appear side by side. At the checked 8:30 frame, the first DFA row includes the new C destination.

segments.title: Complete the new row and draw the DFA
notes: B still loops on 0 and 1. Add a C row with C in both columns, then draw the start arrow at A and accepting marker at B.
The output has three states, but it recognizes exactly the first NFA’s language. Added state count is a consequence of making every transition explicit, not a change in the accepted words.
segments.speakerNotes: Kumpletuhin ang row ng B at ang dalawang self-loops ng C. Pareho pa rin ang language, pero may explicit na rejecting branch na ang DFA.
segments.visualDescription: At checked 9:30 the C row is added; by 10:30–11:30 the DFA graph is drawn alongside the completed table.

segments.title: Example 2: one input can leave two possibilities
notes: The second source NFA starts at A, which loops on 0 and 1. There is also a 1-edge A→B, and B is accepting with no outgoing edges.

For input 1 from A, the destination set is {A,B}. Keeping the A possibility permits more input; the B possibility accepts when the word ends at that point. The NFA recognizes binary words ending in 1.
segments.speakerNotes: Sa pangalawang NFA, may loop sa A at may 1-arrow papunta sa final B. Kaya sa input 1, parehong A at B ang posibleng states.
segments.visualDescription: The second example’s enlarged graph is visible in the checked 12:30 frame. The source briefly revisits the previous table before returning to this example.

segments.title: Build the singleton and composite rows
notes: Begin at subset {A}, displayed simply as A. Its 0-destination is {A}; its 1-destination is {A,B}, written AB as one DFA state.
AB is a label for the subset {A,B}, not an input word and not a simultaneous choice between two DFA nodes.
segments.speakerNotes: Ang AB ay isang DFA state na kumakatawan sa set na A at B. Hindi ito dalawang sunod na input symbols.
segments.visualDescription: The checked 14:30–16:30 frames show A’s NFA destination set and the new AB row in the DFA table.

segments.title: Union the transitions of every subset member
notes: From AB on 0, take δ(A,0)∪δ(B,0)={A}∪∅={A}. From AB on 1, take {A,B}∪∅={A,B}.
AB is accepting because it contains original final state B. The two DFA states A and AB are enough; ∅ is not reachable in this example, so no new trap is required.
segments.speakerNotes: Para sa AB, pagsamahin ang destinations mula A at B. Sa 0, A ang sagot; sa 1, AB. Final ang AB dahil kasama ang final state B.
segments.visualDescription: At checked 17:30 the source writes the union calculation; by 18:30 the two DFA rows are complete.

segments.title: Example 3: reconstruct the input NFA from its tuple and table
notes: The third source NFA uses Q={A,B,C}, Σ={a,b}, start A, and F={C}. Its rows are A:[{A,B},{C}], B:[{A},{B}], C:[∅,{A,B}].
The NFA graph is built from those cells: A has an a-loop and an a-edge to B, A has b→C, B has a→A and a b-loop, and C has b-edges to A and B.
segments.speakerNotes: Sa third example, A ang start at C ang final. Basahin ang given table: A sa a ay A at B, A sa b ay C; B sa a ay A at sa b ay B; C sa a ay empty at sa b ay A at B.
segments.visualDescription: The checked 19:30 frame introduces Example 3, 20:30 shows its tuple/table, and 21:30–22:30 progressively adds the graph’s edges.

segments.title: Process A, then the newly discovered AB
notes: The DFA row for singleton A is a→AB and b→C. AB is new, so add its row rather than leaving it as two separate states.
AB on a gives {A,B}∪{A}={A,B}; AB on b gives {C}∪{B}={B,C}. This discovers another subset, BC.
segments.speakerNotes: Mula A, a ay AB at b ay C. Para sa bagong AB row, union ang gamitin: sa a ay AB; sa b ay BC.
segments.visualDescription: At checked 23:30–24:30, the DFA table gains the A and AB rows while the unions are written below it.
workedSteps: Δ(AB,b)=BC; add BC as a new row.

segments.title: Process BC and C without skipping empty sets
notes: BC on a gives δ(B,a)∪δ(C,a)={A}∪∅={A}. BC on b gives {B}∪{A,B}={A,B}.
C on a has no NFA destination, so the source assigns D to represent ∅. C on b gives AB. D therefore becomes a required reachable trap state.
segments.speakerNotes: Sa BC, a ay A at b ay AB. Sa C, walang a-destination kaya kailangan ng dead state D; sa b ay AB.
segments.visualDescription: The checked 25:30 frame fills BC’s row; by 26:30 C’s a-transition introduces D.

segments.title: Complete D and mark the accepting subsets
notes: D loops on a and b. The five reachable DFA states are A, AB, BC, C, and D.
Only C and BC contain original final state C, so only those two are accepting. AB contains B but not C and is not accepting in this third example. Final labels must be recomputed for each example.
segments.speakerNotes: Kumpletuhin ang D row gamit ang D sa parehong inputs. C at BC ang final dito, dahil C ang original final state sa third example.
segments.visualDescription: The checked 27:30 frame has the full table; around 28:30 the source draws the nodes and accepting markers.

segments.title: Draw the final DFA and cross-check its table
notes: Translate each completed cell into one directed edge. The recreated figure includes all ten state–symbol transitions, including D’s two sink loops.
Check ab: A→AB→BC, so accept. Check bb: A→C→AB, so reject. These traces use the same language as the original NFA, but the DFA has a unique run.
segments.speakerNotes: Pagkatapos makumpleto ang table, iguhit ang bawat transition at i-check ang accepting states. Gamitin ang parehong inputs para maikumpara ang NFA at DFA.
segments.visualDescription: The checked 29:30 frame draws the final DFA from its table. The recreation completes every listed cell explicitly.

recap: A DFA state represents a reachable subset of NFA states.
Union the transitions from every member, then add newly reached subsets.
A subset is accepting if it contains any original accepting state.
An empty subset is a rejecting sink when reachable.
Recompute accepting subsets for each example; the original final state may change.
commonMistakes: Following only one branch from a subset.
Confusing a DFA subset node with one NFA state.
Forgetting to process newly discovered subsets.
Marking a subset final only when all members are final.
Dropping a reachable empty subset from a complete DFA.
Leaving an edge absent where a complete DFA requires a trap transition.

questions.prompt: What must an NFA-to-DFA conversion preserve?
questions.explanation: Equivalence concerns the recognized language, not state count or layout.

questions.prompt: In Source Example 1, what is the NFA destination from A on 1?
questions.explanation: A has a 0-edge to B, but no 1-edge.

questions.prompt: Why is state C added in Source Example 1’s DFA?
choices: To represent the empty destination set and complete missing transitions
questions.explanation: C names the empty subset and loops on both symbols.

questions.prompt: Which word is accepted by Source Example 1’s completed DFA?
questions.explanation: The first 0 reaches B and all later symbols loop there.

questions.prompt: Why is the second source NFA not a DFA?
choices: A has two destinations on symbol 1
It has only one final state
questions.explanation: The 1-loop keeps A while the 1-edge reaches B, giving {A,B}.

questions.prompt: In Source Example 2, what is Δ({A},1)?
questions.explanation: Union every 1-destination from A: the loop gives A and the other edge gives B.

questions.prompt: In Source Example 2, what is Δ({A,B},0)?
Why is AB accepting in Source Example 2?
choices: It contains the start state A
It contains the original final state B
questions.explanation: At least one accepting member is sufficient.

questions.prompt: In Source Example 3, what is Δ(AB,b)?
questions.explanation: Union δ(A,b)={C} with δ(B,b)={B} to obtain {B,C}.

questions.prompt: In Source Example 3, what is Δ(BC,a)?
questions.explanation: δ(B,a)={A} and δ(C,a)=∅, so the union is {A}.

questions.prompt: Which DFA states are accepting in Source Example 3?
questions.explanation: The original final set is {C}; exactly the reachable subsets containing C are accepting.

questions.prompt: In Source Example 3, where does D go on input b?
questions.explanation: D represents ∅, so no symbol can produce a nonempty destination set.

questions.prompt: How many reachable DFA states does Source Example 3 produce before minimization?
questions.explanation: The worklist discovers A, AB, BC, C and the empty subset D; it does not need all 2³ possible subsets.

questions.prompt: What does the label AB represent in a subset DFA?
choices: An input string that must be read next
Proof that A and B are equivalent NFA states
One DFA state representing the subset {A,B}
questions.explanation: Subset construction tracks possibilities; it does not assert that its members are equivalent or merged by minimization.

questions.prompt: Starting at A in Source Example 3’s DFA, what happens on ab?
questions.explanation: The a-column sends A to AB and the b-column sends AB to accepting BC.

provenance: Reconstructed from readable full-video samples at 60-second intervals (sample centers 0:30, 1:30, …, 29:30), with additional table/graph checks. Segment links are approximate navigation points, not exact word boundaries. English explanations, Taglish paraphrases and questions are newly written. Source diagrams are recreated; no original video or full transcript is hosted.
